chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who pronounced Zahaar from his wife, then divorced her before he copulated with her, so she became irrevocably divorced from him. Is there an expiation upon him? He (He) said: No.

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Zahaar, a specific form of divorce in Islamic jurisprudence where a man likens his wife to his mother, requiring expiation.
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation or compensation, typically involving freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding the poor, required for specific acts like Zahaar.
key_terms.يُوَاقِعَهَا: He copulates with her / consummates the marriage.

ai.seo_question: Is the expiation for Zahaar required if the husband divorces his wife before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the expiation (kaffarah) for Zahaar is waived if the husband divorces his wife before consummation, as the condition for the penalty is not fully met. This ruling highlights the juristic principle that Zahaar creates a specific prohibition requiring expiation to resume marital relations, which is resolved or rendered unnecessary through divorce prior to intercourse. The discussion underscores the interplay between marital status and ritual obligations in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Al Aa’la, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about a man who did Zahaar from his wife, then divorced her before he copulated with her. So she was irrevocably divorced from him. Is there an expiation upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 35. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from al-‘ Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who expresses the statement of al- Zihar about his wife, then divorces her before going to bed with her until she becomes stranger to him: if he owes expiation. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, expiation is not obligatory on him.’”
